risks: The Company is exposed to credit, liquidity and interest rate risk.
Investment in Stock Market, both in Quoted and Unquoted Shares, have the risk of change in the price and value, both in term of up and down and thus can affect the profitability of the Company.
Market risk - quoted investments exposed to fluctuations in stock prices
Liquidity and interest rate risk - lending and investment periods may differ from funding sources; volatility in interest rates could cause margins to decline and profitability to shrink
Frequent policy updates, evolving compliance norms, and delays in land acquisition and statutory approvals can extend project timelines and increase holding costs
Natural disasters, pandemics, and macroeconomic disruptions can interrupt construction activity, disrupt supply chains, and weaken demand sentiment
Milestone-based payments, extended receivable cycles, and retention clauses create uneven cash flows, increasing dependence on short-term borrowings and raising finance costs
Lower adoption of advanced construction technologies such as BIM, prefabrication, and digital project management tools can lead to inefficiencies, rework, and margin pressures
Volatility in steel, cement, fuel, and other raw material prices driven by global commodity cycles and currency fluctuations can compress margins, particularly in fixed-price contracts
The Company does not deal into any commodity and hence is not directly exposed to any commodity price risk.
The Company does not enter into any Foreign Exchange transactions and hence is not directly exposed to any Foreign Exchange Risk.

outlook.statement: India's real GDP growth for FY26 estimated at 7.6%, anchored in robust manufacturing performance and resilient domestic demand despite external headwinds.
Headline inflation plummeted to an average of ~2.1% for FY26 (vs. 4.6% in FY25), driven by prolonged nine-month decline in food prices and favourable monsoon.
RBI delivered one of the sharpest easing cycles in recent history, cutting policy rates by a full percentage point within four months starting February 2025, and another 25 bps cut in December 2025.
Central Government set to narrow fiscal gap to 4.4% of GDP for FY26 compared to 4.8% in FY25.
FDI into India grew 18% year-on-year to US$47.87 Bn during April-December FY26; FPI outflows about US$16.4 Bn (up to March 25, 2026), highest ever in any financial year.
Indian construction market size estimated at USD 0.79 trillion in 2026, expected to reach USD 1.10 trillion by 2031 at CAGR 6.87% (2026-2031).

Indian equities transitioned from sustained outperformance to correction and recalibration; valuation over global peers compressed, FPI ownership fallen, reducing crowding risk and improving medium-term risk-reward.

Equity outlook hinges on robust macro backdrop - fastest-growing major economy, low and stable inflation, healthy bank and corporate balance sheets, and breadth of earnings growth beyond a handful of sectors.

India's housing demand gaining momentum due to rapid urbanisation, shifting demographics towards nuclear families, rising aspirations and expanding pool of first-time buyers; demand outlook remains strong aided by economic recovery, accommodative mortgage rates, price stability and growth in household incomes.
